title: Remove owner-specific disclosures and make setup portable
description:
## Goal and context

Make the repository suitable for public use: remove owner-specific infrastructure and identifying details from the current tracked tree, and enable a new operator to configure and run the MCP server with their own VisoMaster Fusion installation. The owner is not treating the details found in the 2026-11-07 audit as an emergency; schedule this work normally. This issue authorizes future implementation when selected, not changes as part of creating the issue.

The audit found no recognizable credentials, private-key headers, common API-token formats, credential-bearing URLs, tracked media, or private IP addresses in its pattern-based scan of the public and local committed history. This is not proof of their absence; repeat an appropriately scoped scan when implementing.

## Privacy scope

- Inventory current tracked files, generated tracker exports, examples, docs, test fixtures and Git metadata for personal usernames, email addresses, local checkout paths, host aliases, filesystem and runtime layouts, hardware inventory, job identifiers, and incidental workstation or media details. Use neutral placeholders and illustrative paths where specifics are not needed for understanding; retain meaningful technical requirements and general reproducible verification evidence. Do not copy the actual identifying values into new documentation or issue text.
- Remove or generalize owner-specific content in README, agent/developer instructions, verification notes, client examples, code defaults, tests and Beads records as appropriate. Check whether Beads automatically reintroduces local absolute source paths or actor identifiers on every export; devise and test a durable, compatible fix rather than only editing the generated JSONL once. Preserve issue IDs, relationships, unrelated records and tracker functionality.
- Review Git author/committer metadata and existing public history separately. Replacing files in a new commit does not erase earlier commits, and clones/caches may persist. Prepare an evidence-based remediation recommendation including consequences and alternatives. Do not rewrite Git history, force-push, change visibility, rotate credentials or alter external accounts without specific authorization at implementation time. Do not declare historical exposure removed merely because HEAD is clean.
- Review ignore rules and examples to reduce accidental future commits of local config, credentials, private media, logs, runtime artifacts and model weights without masking legitimate source files; document checks and exceptions.

## Portability scope

- Inventory every assumption spanning the client, deployment, remote control and GPU worker. Define a coherent configuration contract for SSH host, remote adapter directory, remote media/base root, Fusion checkout, runtime state, GPU selection, runner and local downloads. Validate paths and reject inconsistent or unsafe configurations with useful errors. Avoid requiring a particular username, home layout, host alias or mount path.
- Document and implement how local VISOMASTER_* configuration and remote VM_* settings reach every noninteractive SSH control invocation, deployment operation and detached supervisor/worker. Test actual propagation and persistence; a variable set only in the local client environment must not be assumed to appear remotely. Keep shell quoting, structured stdin, media/artifact root confinement and existing SSH security properties intact.
- Replace the undocumented installation-specific runner dependency with a configurable and documented launcher or a portable supported equivalent. Provide instructions or an example for configuring a Fusion Python environment, GPU libraries and model assets, and make failures actionable. Preserve the currently qualified installation via a documented migration/compatibility path; do not silently change its CUDA environment, GPU selection, job state or deployment paths.
- Provide a clean, reproducible setup guide from clone through dependencies, SSH configuration, Fusion revision, FFmpeg/FFprobe, deployment, client registration, health/settings checks, face detection, preview and short render. Use neutral examples, explain how to adapt them, state the supported Linux/NVIDIA and client-platform assumptions, and clearly identify prerequisites versus optional features. Make client example paths placeholders rather than claims of ready-to-use configuration.
- Document the exact Fusion revision guard and process for qualifying other revisions and hardware; do not remove or relax the guard without equivalent adapter and GPU qualification. Document the limits of existing GPU validation. Clarify the source-checkout assumption for code-match checks, or package the needed files if a distributable installation is supported.
- Select and add a project license only after an authorized owner decision; separately identify upstream Fusion and model-weight license and redistribution restrictions. Do not imply that a public repository automatically grants usage rights or that the project's license overrides upstream terms.

## Compatibility, verification and acceptance criteria

- [ ] A deliberate, repeatable audit of the current tracked tree and exported tracker state finds no owner-specific identifiers or infrastructure details within the agreed cleanup scope; examples use consistent placeholders and a fresh Beads mutation/export does not reintroduce excluded metadata.
- [ ] The issue/report distinguishes current-tree cleanup from historical Git and GitHub metadata, records remaining exposure and identifies any history rewrite as a separately authorized decision.
- [ ] One documented configuration works with non-default local and remote paths, a non-default SSH alias and a non-default runner; all required settings are visible to control, detached supervisor and GPU worker, including after reconnect. Invalid/inconsistent paths fail clearly and safely.
- [ ] Existing installation users have documented upgrade steps, and existing tool names/schemas, durable jobs, stable IDs, concurrency/GPU locking, cancellation, artifact isolation and deployment safety remain compatible unless an explicitly documented migration is necessary.
- [ ] Local automated tests cover custom configuration propagation, quoting and path validation, generated examples, Beads export behavior where practical, and existing protocol/job regressions. Run the repository's full required checks and document any gaps.
- [ ] Follow the new instructions from a clean or isolated non-default setup through registration, health/settings and deployment; record the exact environment and results. Run a short detection/preview/render on appropriately authorized hardware when available, or explicitly leave that qualification outstanding rather than claim full end-to-end portability.
- [ ] Public documentation states supported platforms, exact Fusion revision, required dependencies/model assets, licensing decisions and tested limitations. Client examples do not contain the owner's path or claim unmodified examples are ready to run.
- [ ] No media, model weights, secrets or runtime artifacts are committed; scan the resulting tracked content and inspect the semantic tracker diff before delivery.
close_reason: Implemented: privacy audit + clean tree, remote-config.json contract reaching control/supervisor/worker, configurable runner, transport validation shared with deploy, portable setup docs, MIT license with upstream terms, neutral Beads actor. Isolated live check and production migration verified (health, config hash, job history, smoke, Claude client). History squash done separately per owner decision.

title: Frame-accurate decode for render and preview
description: OpenCV CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES seeking (engine.py render_video, load_frame) is not guaranteed frame-accurate for long-GOP codecs while audio offset is computed exactly from start_frame/fps, risking A/V desync. Decode through an FFmpeg pipe with accurate seeking (or sequential decode) so decode and encode share one timing model. Qualify start_frame>0 on GPU with A/V alignment evidence.
close_reason: Merged: packet-pts timing check bounded to range (200s 720p: 39.5s→1.06s); FFmpeg-pipe exact-index decode (bit-identical vs sequential at 25 indices, live start_frame=30 render A/V lag 0.0ms); progress fps/ETA.

title: Atomic versioned deployment with hash reporting
description: deploy.sh overwrites live files that queued jobs load at start. Deploy to versioned directories and switch a symlink atomically; refuse while non-terminal jobs exist unless forced; have health_check report deployed file hashes so the Mac can detect code mismatch.
close_reason: Merged: versioned releases + atomic symlink swap, active-job refusal, release pinning test, health_check code hashes/code_matches. Dev-target live test passed incl. migration and pinning.

title: Document project-specific agent workflow in AGENTS.md
description: Ground agent instructions in current architecture, runtime constraints, checks, deployment workflow and Beads/Git conventions. Validate the document, commit and push.
close_reason: Added AGENTS.md grounded in current runtime boundaries, job invariants, local/GPU checks, deployment workflow and Beads/Git delivery rules. Validated 14 paths, Python/SDK declarations and smoke-test flags against source.

title: Expose best-match swapping to stop non-target identity flicker
description: Tracking qualification (tracking-base-l1) showed the non-target woman swapped on 51/96 frames at default SimilarityThreshold 60; threshold 75 removed it. Adapter forces SwapOnlyBestMatchEnableToggle off. Qualify exposing/enabling best-match and/or guidance on threshold, and document it in submit_swap.

title: Preserve 10-bit/HDR sources in render output
description: Output is always 8-bit yuv420p CRF 18. Preserve 10-bit and color metadata (or expose quality/codec options). Requires GPU qualification.
close_reason: Merged: explicit source matrix/range on decode+encode with accurate rounding, color tags preserved, 10-bit sources encoded High 10, PQ/HLG rejected. Identity round trip +4 dB PSNR, -2 level shift removed; live 24-frame renders of a 10-bit BT.709 clip and an 8-bit BT.601 limited-range clip.

title: Late cancel must not discard a completed render
description: control.py supervise checks the cancel marker before success, so a cancel arriving just after successful exit marks the job cancelled and withholds artifacts. Prefer success when returncode==0 and result.json exists. Add a regression test.
close_reason: Merged 4c6fd77/418d9a8 equivalents: engine error.json surfaced as state.error; success preferred over late cancel. Tests + live failed-job check passed.

title: Job deletion, retention pruning and upload dedup
description: jobs/ and uploads/ grow without bound (uploads up to 20 GiB). Add delete_job tool (terminal jobs only), age-based pruning, and content-hash dedup for uploads.
close_reason: Merged: delete_job, prune_storage (dry-run default), content-addressed uploads with remote sha256 check. Live scratch-state prune/delete and dedup (0.94s→0.09s) verified.

title: Labelled contact sheet of detected faces
description: Produce one labelled image of all detected face crops so the agent needs one view_artifact call.
close_reason: Merged: detect_faces sample_frames/frames (≤64) with embedding clustering at Fusion's default similarity threshold, verified representative crops, labelled contact.jpg. description: Multi-frame detect clusters at fixed Fusion default 60, splitting profile views (one identity on a three-person clip). Add an optional clustering threshold. Also list_jobs summaries show only 'frame' for detect jobs, not sample_frames/frames.

description: Job error is only 'Worker exited with code N'; the real exception is buried in log_tail. Engine should persist its exception (e.g. error.json) and the supervisor should publish it in state.error.

title: Report per-identity swap coverage and suspicious render intervals
description:
## Problem and intended result
A render currently records an aggregate swap count and fails when that total is zero. A positive total does not establish that every requested mapping was used or that swaps remained consistent throughout the clip. Provide a compact per-mapping report plus review artifacts so an operator can find partial failures without watching the entire output.

## Scope
Instrument the actual Fusion matching and swapping path to attribute observations to stable mapping IDs. Capture processed frames, detected candidates, eligible matches, successful swaps, available similarity scores, and ambiguous candidates. Group suspicious observations into source-frame intervals with timestamps and a bounded number of before/after review images. Keep the full report as a versioned JSON artifact and expose a small summary through job_status/result metadata.

Distinguish an observed failure from absence or uncertainty: a frame with no matching face does not prove that the intended person should have been visible. Coverage denominators and any user-supplied expected-visible intervals must be explicit. Define ambiguity rules using observed candidate scores; do not invent scores or equate similarity with visual quality. Default reports are advisory. Optional strict thresholds must be explicit and preserve existing job terminal-state semantics.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on vmcp-accurate-seek-7bz so reported source frames, timestamps and review images correspond to actual decoded output. The multi-frame discovery and tracking beads are related but not prerequisites: this feature works with today's explicit mappings and independent per-frame matching. It does not implement temporal tracking, automatic identity assignment or a universal aesthetic score. Keep telemetry bounded and avoid recomputing inference solely to manufacture metrics.

## Validation and delivery
Use deterministic matching fixtures for counters and interval logic, then qualify a short multi-person GPU clip with one deliberately unmatched mapping and one partially matched mapping. Record exact job IDs, configuration, representative report excerpts, performance observations and limitations in VERIFICATION.md. Update README/schema discovery only for public interface changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A versioned report identifies each requested mapping and records observed detection/match/swap counts with documented denominators; an unused mapping cannot disappear into the aggregate total.
- [ ] Missing detections, below-threshold matches, ambiguous candidates and processing errors are distinguishable where the installed Fusion path exposes that evidence; unavailable evidence is marked unknown.
- [ ] Suspicious intervals use zero-based source-frame ranges with a documented end convention and rational-FPS-derived timestamps, including renders with start_frame > 0.
- [ ] Review images are labelled with mapping ID, frame/time and reason, have a configurable bounded count, and remain inside the owning job's artifact directory.
- [ ] A render in which one identity swaps and another never matches produces an explicit per-identity warning. No-face intervals alone are not asserted to be failures.
- [ ] Optional expected-visible intervals and strict coverage thresholds are validated and recorded. Existing all-zero-swap failure behavior remains intact; advisory warnings do not invent a new terminal status.
- [ ] Status responses remain compact; detailed reports are downloadable. Failed/cancelled work cannot publish a complete-success report.
- [ ] Regression tests cover multiple mappings, unused mappings, ambiguous matches, gaps, nonzero start offsets, report limits and failed processing. Short GPU qualification verifies telemetry against inspected frames and documents overhead.

title: Compare labelled preview variants across identical frames and short clips
description:
## Problem and intended result
Choosing swap, mask and restoration parameters currently requires separately submitting previews and manually correlating each artifact with its settings. Add a bounded comparison job that runs named parameter variants against the same explicit frames or short excerpt and returns directly comparable results.

## Scope
Accept a common media path, explicit target/source mappings and frame selection plus uniquely named variants with validated parameter/control overrides. Produce a labelled original-versus-variant image grid for selected stills and, for a short clip, equal-range comparison outputs with a common frame/time basis. Include a machine-readable manifest containing each variant's fully resolved settings, source frames, outcome and artifact references. Provide a copyable submit_swap request for the selected variant; selection remains with the user/agent.

Choose a small documented limit on variants, frames, clip length and output dimensions to prevent accidentally scheduling an unbounded sweep. Preserve durable submission, reconnect, conflict rejection, cancellation and the shared GPU lock. Reuse existing inference paths; optimize model reuse only if measured and qualified without compromising job isolation.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on vmcp-accurate-seek-7bz: comparing different decoded frames would make a settings comparison misleading. vmcp-contact-sheet-fk3 concerns discovered face crops; share layout utilities if available, but do not make that feature a blocker. Quality-report annotations can be integrated later and are not required for the initial comparison workflow. Do not add automatic best-setting selection or unrestricted hyperparameter search.

## Validation and delivery
Cover variant validation and lifecycle through local/stdio tests. Qualify at least two variants across the same frontal/profile or expression-changing excerpt on the supported GPU. Inspect labels, settings manifests, frame alignment and any audio-bearing clip outputs. Record evidence and tool-discovery/documentation changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One durable request accepts bounded named variants and explicit sample frames or a bounded contiguous clip, with duplicate variant names, invalid overrides and over-limit work rejected before rendering.
- [ ] Every variant receives the same source frames, mappings and common settings except for its recorded overrides; rational frame rate and start offsets are preserved.
- [ ] Still comparisons include the original and clearly labelled variants. Layout/downscaling preserves aspect ratio and provides separate full-resolution artifacts for inspection.
- [ ] Clip variants use the same range, frame count, duration and documented audio policy; any synchronized composite must not offset variants or duplicate audio.
- [ ] The manifest records resolved settings and outcome per variant, and can supply a valid single-variant follow-up submission without reconstructing settings from image labels.
- [ ] A variant failure is visible with its reason. Partial outputs are never presented as an entirely successful comparison; the documented parent/child result policy respects existing terminal-state and artifact rules.
- [ ] Identical stable-ID retries return existing work, changed requests conflict, reconnect exposes progress, and cancellation stops owned work without leaving orphan variants or bypassing the GPU lock.
- [ ] Local tests cover limits, settings inheritance, deterministic ordering, manifest/artifact integrity and failure/cancellation. GPU evidence confirms identical input alignment and visibly attributable variant results.

title: Assess reference-image quality and support explicit source weights
description:
## Problem and intended result
Reference setup checks that each image contains exactly one detected face, then averages all source embeddings equally. A tiny, blurry, duplicate or wrong-identity reference can therefore weaken a source collection without a useful explanation. Add an inspectable reference-analysis workflow and explicit inclusion/weight controls.

## Scope
Analyze the exact image bytes and detected face crop used by the configured recognition/swap models. Return labelled crops, face count/size, a documented blur or sharpness measure, duplicate indicators and embedding-consistency/outlier evidence within the supplied collection. Treat embedding outliers as uncertainty requiring review rather than asserting a person's identity.

Allow the caller to exclude a reference or assign nonnegative weights and compute the normalized weighted embedding using the installed Fusion-compatible path. Preserve today's list-of-paths behavior as equal weights. Do not silently drop, replace or rebalance images. A chosen selection/weight set must be reproducible in subsequent previews/renders and their manifests.

Use a queued GPU analysis stage where recognition is necessary; inexpensive file checks can run immediately. Reuse the shared GPU lock and path validation. Return bounded summaries and crops without exposing raw embeddings unnecessarily.

## Boundaries and relationships
This P1 issue can start independently. Multi-frame identity discovery analyzes target footage and is not a prerequisite. Readiness checks will reuse this analysis, and render recipes will retain selected references/weights; neither should block implementation here. Existing exactly-one-face errors remain explicit.

## Validation and delivery
Test validation and weighting with deterministic embeddings and image fixtures. GPU-qualify a collection containing clear same-source images, a blurred/tiny image and a deliberately unrelated synthetic reference. Record observed warnings and limitations; do not claim universal quality thresholds from one fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each supplied reference has a stable identifier, labelled crop when valid, face-count result and actionable quality findings; unreadable, zero-face and multi-face files are explicit.
- [ ] Sharpness/face-size metrics state units, crop basis and configurable thresholds. Outlier scores state their recognition model and comparison basis and are unavailable rather than fabricated for insufficient evidence.
- [ ] Duplicate or strongly redundant images are identified where determinable. Single-image collections remain valid and do not receive unsupported consistency conclusions.
- [ ] No analysis silently removes or edits a reference. Exclusions and weights require explicit request data and are returned in the resolved configuration.
- [ ] Weights must be finite and nonnegative, match the selected references, and have a positive sum. The embedding is normalized consistently with the qualified Fusion path.
- [ ] Omitting weights preserves the current equal-average behavior; a single selected reference reproduces the corresponding single-reference result within an appropriate numeric tolerance.
- [ ] Subsequent swap requests use the exact selected reference bytes and weights or detect that the analyzed inputs changed; analysis results are not blindly reused after content/model changes.
- [ ] Tests cover weighting, all-zero/negative/nonfinite/mismatched weights, duplicates, missing/multiple faces, outliers and changed inputs. Short GPU qualification verifies warnings and weighted preview behavior.
- [ ] Public schemas, compatibility behavior, report artifacts and operational limits are documented and exercised through stdio tests.

title: Preflight a swap request with actionable readiness and qualification results
description:
## Problem and intended result
An operator currently assembles readiness information from health_check, get_settings, inspect_media and trial jobs. Add a request-specific preflight that explains whether the proposed swap can start, which checks remain unverified and how to resolve concrete blockers before scheduling a long render.

## Scope
Accept the same normalized swap intent as submission: media/range, mappings, controls and parameters. Check path access, request/settings validity, render-media compatibility, selected model files/dependencies, output-storage writability/free space, adapter/Fusion compatibility and known qualification evidence. Reuse reference analysis for an optional queued GPU stage. Cheap checks must not load models or occupy the GPU; expensive stages must use normal job lifecycle and locking.

Return structured checks with stable codes, severity, evidence, suggested actions and a checked-at/input/configuration fingerprint. Distinguish validated, blocked, warning and not-checked results. Report qualification as evidence for a particular hardware/model/configuration combination with a date and source; an allowed setting is not automatically qualified.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on vmcp-vfr-check-4jw so media timing inspection is bounded by the requested work rather than decoding an entire long video, and on vmcp-harden-pqj.3 (reference checks) for optional reference analysis. vmcp-normalize-oll is a recovery action to recommend when available, not a prerequisite or an automatic side effect. Disk/VRAM availability are observations or estimates, not reservations or guarantees. Submission must revalidate mutable prerequisites.

## Validation and delivery
Exercise missing files/models, stale revisions, invalid ranges/settings, incompatible media, insufficient space and unknown qualification through mocked/local fixtures and actual stdio calls. Verify a cheap preflight does not start GPU inference or modify inputs. Qualify the optional GPU stage using the reference-analysis fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The API accepts a real swap request shape and shares normalization/validation with submission so a separately maintained permissive schema cannot drift.
- [ ] The response has a documented overall readiness result and per-check codes, severities, evidence and corrective actions; skipped checks and missing qualification evidence are explicit.
- [ ] Cheap checks cover media/range suitability, supported settings, required model assets, paths/storage and code/revision compatibility without loading GPU models.
- [ ] Optional reference analysis runs as durable queued work under the shared GPU lock, with idempotent submission, cancellation and reconnect support.
- [ ] Qualification records identify the tested model/settings/hardware and evidence date; untested allowed combinations are labelled unqualified rather than rejected solely for lacking evidence.
- [ ] Timing inspection uses the range-limited validation path. Rejected media can suggest normalization without silently transcoding or changing the request.
- [ ] Reports fingerprint the inputs/configuration and record check time. Submission rechecks mutable conditions and does not treat a successful preflight as a resource reservation.
- [ ] Tests verify invalid/missing assets, unsupported combinations, low storage, changed inputs and unknown qualification, plus stdio discovery/schema behavior and no inference during cheap checks.

title: Save reusable render recipes with resolved settings and input provenance
description:
## Problem and intended result
Jobs persist submitted requests, but paths and partial overrides do not fully describe a reproducible configuration. Add versioned named recipes that capture resolved settings, explicit identity mappings and content/version provenance, then safely instantiate a new job or adapt a recipe to a new clip.

## Scope
Create a recipe from explicit intent or a completed job. Record effective controls/parameters, source and target reference fingerprints, selected reference weights when supported, source media fingerprint, frame-range convention, Fusion revision, deployed adapter release/hash and relevant model identifiers/checksums. Keep a schema version and immutable recipe revisions so editing a name does not change historical executions.

Support inspecting/exporting a recipe and creating a new render request with explicit substitutions. Applying a recipe to a new clip requires an explicit target-reference/mapping and range decision; do not assume a target from an unrelated clip is valid. Record substitutions and the parent recipe revision in the new job. Provide a readable diff when input content, defaults, model assets or code versions changed.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on the closed vmcp-atomic-deploy-5px for stable release identity and on vmcp-cleanup-u2q for a defined retention/dedup contract. A saved recipe must either retain referenced assets safely or report unavailable inputs; pruning cannot silently break a protected recipe. Use content-addressed assets or verified fingerprints without creating an unrestricted file export mechanism. Reference weights integrate with vmcp-harden-pqj.3 (reference checks) when available, but basic recipes support today's equal weights and need not wait for that feature.

Do not promise bit-for-bit GPU determinism or redistribute model weights. Portable export contains configuration/provenance and optional explicitly selected media within allowed roots. Keep artifact storage outside tracked source.

## Validation and delivery
Round-trip recipes through serialization and stdio, test changed inputs/defaults/models, and verify cleanup interactions and atomic revision writes. Use a short known preview to demonstrate a recipe's resolved configuration produces equivalent behavior with recorded limits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A versioned recipe format stores effective settings, mappings, reference selection/weights, input content fingerprints and code/model provenance, rather than only paths and caller overrides.
- [ ] Named recipes resolve to immutable revisions; concurrent creation/update cannot overwrite an existing revision or produce partial JSON.
- [ ] Inspect/export/import validates schema, allowed paths and integrity. Unsupported versions or missing dependencies produce actionable errors without silently substituting defaults.
- [ ] A recipe can produce a new explicit swap request; media/target/range substitutions are recorded and validated, and the execution manifest identifies its parent recipe revision.
- [ ] Changed file bytes at the same path, changed model assets or changed adapter/Fusion versions are detected and surfaced before reuse; metadata alone is not accepted as content identity.
- [ ] Large-file hashing is streamed and performed at deliberate creation/execution boundaries, not on every status poll.
- [ ] Retention/pruning honors owned retained assets or explicit pinning. Missing unretained assets are reported; deleting a recipe cannot delete assets still referenced by another recipe or active job.
- [ ] Round-trip, concurrent revision, tampering, missing asset, path containment and retention regressions pass. A documented preview reproduction records exact configuration and avoids unsupported claims of bitwise determinism.

title: Apply explicit mappings and parameter overrides by shot or frame range
description:
## Problem and intended result
A submission currently applies one mapping collection and parameter set throughout a contiguous render range. Edited footage may need a different threshold or restoration setting for a profile shot, a replacement identity only during selected shots, or an intentionally untouched section. Add an explicit frame-range plan for one render while preserving the original timeline.

## Scope
Accept a base configuration plus a bounded ordered set of source-frame segments using a documented half-open convention [start_frame, end_frame). Each segment may replace the active mappings, override allowed parameters/controls or request passthrough. Define gap behavior explicitly (base settings or passthrough); reject ambiguous overlap rather than silently choosing a winner. title: Checkpoint validated render chunks and resume interrupted work safely
description:
## Problem and intended result
Detached jobs survive client disconnects, but a worker/workstation interruption during a long render can still require all frames to be processed again. Add validated chunk checkpoints and an explicit resume operation that reuses completed work only when the full render configuration and inputs match.

## Scope
Partition an intended render into deterministic source-frame chunks. Publish each checkpoint atomically only after checking its frame count/range, timing and integrity. Maintain a versioned durable manifest recording committed chunks and configuration/content provenance. On recovery, ignore incomplete writes and verify candidate chunks before reuse.

Resume creates a new linked attempt with a new stable job ID; it must preserve the historical failed/cancelled attempt and idempotency/conflict semantics. Caller cancellation never triggers automatic restart. Retry only missing or invalid chunks, then assemble and validate the final output. Preserve audio timing over the entire requested interval and avoid gaps, duplicate frames and repeated lossy encodes during assembly.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on vmcp-accurate-seek-7bz for exact chunk boundaries, vmcp-cleanup-u2q for retention ownership/pinning, and vmcp-harden-pqj.5 (render recipes) for content/configuration/version provenance. Reuse that fingerprint contract rather than maintaining a second incompatible one. The tracking bead is related: future temporal state must be checkpointed or deterministically reconstructed with qualified overlap/warm-up. Until supported, reject resume combinations that cannot preserve temporal semantics.

This issue does not add automatic retry of deterministic processing failures, a distributed worker system or priority preemption. Keep the existing owned-process cancellation, GPU lease and release pinning invariants.

## Validation and delivery
Inject failures during chunk encoding, checkpoint publication, final assembly and supervisor recovery. Compare an uninterrupted run with a resumed run for frame identity/timing and visible boundary artifacts. Perform a short GPU interruption/resume test before claiming long-render readiness; record remaining reboot/long-run gaps separately.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A durable versioned checkpoint manifest identifies the complete requested range, provenance fingerprint, committed chunk ranges and integrity data.
- [ ] Partial or corrupt chunks are never trusted. Publication/reconciliation is atomic and handles interruption before/after both artifact and manifest writes.
- [ ] Explicit resume produces a new linked job attempt and preserves prior terminal state; identical resume retries are idempotent and changed intent conflicts.
- [ ] Input/reference bytes, effective settings, model assets, Fusion/adapter version and relevant runtime compatibility are checked before reuse. Mismatches fail with an explanation or require a fresh render.
- [ ] Only validated compatible chunks are reused. Missing/invalid ranges are reprocessed without duplicate/missing output frames, and concurrent resume requests cannot corrupt shared checkpoints.
- [ ] Final assembly preserves frame count, source order, FPS, dimensions, duration and audio alignment; it avoids repeated lossy re-encoding of completed video chunks.
- [ ] Active/resumable chunks and required releases/assets follow an explicit cleanup retention contract; pruning cannot remove files leased by a resume attempt.
- [ ] Tracking/temporal configurations are either restored/reconstructed with qualified boundary continuity or rejected explicitly; no silent state reset masquerades as equivalent recovery.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests cover checkpoint and assembly crash windows, stale state, corrupt chunks, cancellation and concurrent resume. GPU evidence compares interrupted/resumed and uninterrupted output at every tested boundary.

title: Schedule GPU jobs predictably with preview priority and starvation protection
description:
## Problem and intended result
Workers currently contend for a shared GPU flock; exclusion is guaranteed but admission order is not. A burst of jobs can make preview turnaround unpredictable. Add durable FIFO ordering within priority classes, an interactive preview class and bounded starvation protection while preserving process isolation.

## Scope
Persist an enqueue sequence/tie-breaker and validated priority class for each job. Choose the next eligible job through one atomic scheduling decision per GPU. Detection/preview requests may use an interactive class, while renders use a normal class by default. Define a concrete fairness rule such as an aging threshold plus maximum consecutive interactive admissions; expose enough state to explain the next choice.

Report advisory queue position, class, wait duration and waiting reason through job_status/list_jobs, including that position may change under the declared policy. Wake long-poll callers when observable queue state changes. Reconnects and duplicate submissions must preserve enqueue identity rather than moving a job forward or backward.

## Boundaries and relationships
Depends on the already-closed vmcp-list-jobs-jas and vmcp-long-poll-wt4 as the public status/list integration bases. vmcp-harden-pqj.7 (checkpoint/resume) is related future work, not a prerequisite. Initial scheduling occurs only between jobs: a running render retains the GPU and cannot be interrupted just to admit a preview.

Do not add multi-GPU placement, distributed queues, GUI-process termination or promises of a start-time ETA. Continue to respect the shared GPU lease, inherited lock and owned-process cancellation. Scheduler recovery must never create two concurrent workers after a crash or reconnect.

## Validation and delivery
Use a deterministic local backend and concurrent submitters to exercise order, aging, duplicate submissions, cancellations and scheduler crashes. Verify that long-poll/status/list output remains bounded. Document fairness precisely enough that tests can predict admission order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Jobs receive a durable enqueue sequence and validated class. FIFO is deterministic within a class, including simultaneous submissions and stable-ID retries.
- [ ] A documented aging/burst-limit rule provides a testable bound on repeated interactive admissions ahead of an eligible normal job; a sustained preview stream cannot starve renders.
- [ ] Selection and GPU admission are atomic across clients/supervisors, and existing mutual exclusion and inherited-lease crash protection remain intact.
- [ ] Queue state exposes class, approximate position, wait duration and reason through compatible status/list schemas; policy-driven position changes are documented.
- [ ] Long polling observes relevant queue changes without spawning busy status loops or attaching unbounded logs to normal responses.
- [ ] Cancelling a queued job removes its eligibility; cancelling an owned running job preserves existing semantics. A late cancel still cannot discard a successful result.
- [ ] Scheduler restart reconciles durable queue/running state without duplicate execution, lost jobs or a fresh enqueue position for retried requests.
- [ ] Priority does not preempt an active render, stop unrelated GPU processes, or imply a promised ETA; later chunk-boundary yielding is explicitly separate.
- [ ] Deterministic concurrency/fairness/crash tests and stdio schema tests pass. README documents classes, fairness, queue-position semantics and the non-preemptive first release.
