title: Resolve the VisoMaster MCP code review findings
description:
## Goal

Resolve the 29 defects identified during the whole-tree review of VisoMaster MCP at commit `ab8753a` on 2026-11-07. The child issues are numbered in review order and each contains its trigger, expected behavior, source references and verification criteria. All file references in the review are relative to the project and refer to that baseline. Recheck the current tree before implementation.

## Scope and evidence

- Findings 1–11 cover media path confinement, exact frame selection, detection reference identity, video/audio duration and presentation, and color and bit-depth handling.
- Findings 12–21 cover durable job identity and retries, cancellation, artifact transfers, storage retention and job reporting.
- Findings 22–29 cover atomic deployment, CPU and path configuration, input validation, compatibility reporting and the smoke check.
- The review used local source inspection, generated FFmpeg fixtures, shell reproductions and temporary job stores. Some scenarios were derived from the code and are marked accordingly in the child issues. Render checks that needed a swap stage used a pass-through stub. Production GPU and native client behavior were outside the review.

## Delivery constraints

Prioritize media confinement, silently incorrect frame selection, unintended deletion and job-generation races. Keep durable IDs and responses compatible, preserve explicit isolation of source media and completed artifacts, and account for two clients and concurrent maintenance operations in the regressions. Use synthetic fixtures, an isolated backend and deterministic scheduling where possible. Keep GPU qualification and deployment separate from local verification. Existing historical issues cover earlier versions of some of these behaviors and remain useful context.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Resolve all 29 direct child bugs and record implementation and verification evidence on each issue.
- [ ] Cover media boundary escapes and silent output errors with generated fixtures and assertions on actual selected frames, tracks or output metadata.
- [ ] Cover retention, transfer, cancellation and deployment races with deterministic concurrent or fault-injected regressions.
- [ ] Run the repository's locked local test and Ruff checks for changes. Record any workstation/GPU qualification performed and any outstanding coverage.
- [ ] Verify all 29 issues remain linked to the epic until resolved, and close the epic after the child acceptance criteria are met.

title: Prevent FFmpeg demuxers from opening media outside the configured root
description:
## Problem

The workstation API validates the top-level file path and then lets FFmpeg and FFprobe auto-detect the demuxer. A media-looking file can actually be a playlist or a concat manifest. Its child paths bypass the workstation path validator, which allows a request to access video the direct path check rejects.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with synthetic FFmpeg fixtures. Create an HLS playlist under `/media/root` that names an existing `/media/outside.ts` segment by absolute path. The normal probe follows the segment. Separately, create `/media/root/concat.mp4` containing an FFconcat header and a relative `file clip.mp4` entry. Point `/media/root/clip.mp4` at a synthetic file outside the root. The direct path is refused, but an otherwise normal render with a pass-through Fusion stub completed and returned frames from the outside file.

`remote/common.py:67-74` resolves and validates only the caller-provided path. `remote/common.py:85-92` probes it by content. `remote/engine.py:152-165`, `remote/engine.py:467-477`, `remote/engine.py:562-574`, and `remote/engine.py:645-651` independently open that same input for decode, timing, audio mux or normalization.

## Implementation notes

Establish one shared input policy for ordinary self-contained image and video formats. Enforce it by content across every FFmpeg and FFprobe entry point, including timing validation and the second input in the render mux. Consider restrictions at the demuxer or process boundary so a nested file opener cannot evade the check. Keep user errors actionable for unsupported manifests and use synthetic files in regression tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An in-root HLS manifest with an out-of-root segment is rejected before that segment can be probed or decoded.
- [ ] A file named concat.mp4 whose contents are an FFconcat manifest cannot probe or render an out-of-root target through a relative symlink.
- [ ] The shared policy also covers timing probes, normalization and the render audio read, including when the top-level file has a supported extension.
- [ ] Representative in-root MP4, MOV, MKV, PNG and JPEG inputs still work through their normal entry points. Direct outside paths and escaping symlinks remain rejected.
close_reason: Fixed in be7f430. common.ffmpeg_input applies -protocol_whitelist file and a self-contained demuxer allowlist to every FFmpeg/FFprobe input (probe, decode, timing, normalize, both render mux inputs); image2 only in ffprobe with -pattern_type none. tests/test_confine.py (17) passes on FFmpeg 8.1 and the workstation's 6.1; 10 fail on the old code. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Handle short clips that resample to zero frames at an accepted FPS
description:
## Problem

Normalization accepts a valid low target frame rate and assumes at least one expected output frame. FFmpeg can round the entire source down to zero frames. The later probe then raises a message implying the input has no video stream.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` by normalizing a 0.2 s, 25 fps H.264 MP4 to 1 fps. The FFmpeg output had no video stream and the job failed with `Media has no video stream`, although the input was valid.

`remote/common.py:164-171` accepts target rates down to 1 fps. `remote/engine.py:653` resamples with the default FPS filter rounding, `remote/engine.py:677-678` expects at least one frame, and `remote/engine.py:708-709` validates the resulting file.

## Implementation notes

Make the accepted-rate contract and resampling behavior agree for clips shorter than a target frame period. Preserve one source frame when this is the chosen normalization policy. If the interval is intentionally rejected, explain how source duration and requested FPS caused the rejection and provide actionable guidance to choose another rate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The 0.2 s source at 1 fps produces a validated one-frame result, or a specific rate-versus-duration error before any artifact is published.
- [ ] A genuinely video-free input still gets its own clear input error.
- [ ] Clips on each side of the rounding boundary and an ordinary downsample verify that frame count and duration remain consistent with the documented policy.
close_reason: Fixed in a777ad8. Policy: keep at least one frame. normalize_command adds eof_action=pass when the estimated extent is under 0.75 frame periods; zero output reports 'Normalization produced no video frames'; video-free input keeps 'Media has no video stream'. test_audio.py covers 0.2/0.48/0.52/1.48/1.52 s at 1 fps and a 25->10 fps downsample. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Verify detection crops contain the intended identity before marking them usable
description:
## Problem

Face crops add padding that can include nearby faces. Single-frame detection returns these crops as target references without rechecking them. Multi-frame detection verifies only the count of detections in the crop, so a crop can be marked verified if the detector finds only a neighboring person. A bad crop can make a later swap fail or bind to the wrong person.

## Reproduction and evidence

Source inference at `ab8753a`. The review did not run Fusion on a live or GPU fixture. Reproduce deterministically by simulating two nearby detections in the full frame. On a padded crop for person A, return either both detections or one detection positioned on person B. Also exercise a later candidate crop that contains only person A.

`remote/engine.py:215-222` creates padded crops. `remote/engine.py:309-328` accepts any single re-detection as verified. `remote/engine.py:763-779` publishes single-frame crop paths without verification. The swap configuration counts detections in `remote/engine.py:367-379`. `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:136-145` describes those paths as usable target references.

## Implementation notes

Reuse the swap reference detector constraints when verifying candidate crops. Establish that the one re-detected face corresponds to the original box or embedding. If the padded crop cannot be verified, try a smaller crop or another candidate within bounded work, and expose failure clearly using a client-compatible manifest and contact-sheet treatment. Keep artifacts available for human inspection where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A deterministic fixture with two people in the padded crop never labels that crop a usable single-face reference.
- [ ] A crop with exactly one re-detection belonging to the neighboring person is treated as unverified. A later candidate containing the intended face can be selected.
- [ ] A clean crop from single-frame detection and multi-frame detection is verified and usable through the same constraints as submit_swap.
- [ ] When all candidates are unverified, the manifest and contact sheet communicate that state and preserve discoverable crop artifacts without advertising them as ready targets.

title: Keep replacement jobs outside the prune snapshot
description:
## Problem

A storage prune can delete a newly completed job that reused the ID of an old job. The replacement's result and artifacts can disappear even though its finish time is inside the requested retention window. The returned record can then carry the finish time of the old job.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced locally against reviewed commit `ab8753a` using isolated state. Seed an old completed job, intercept the call from `prune` to `delete_job` after selection, delete the old directory, then create a newly completed job with the same ID and a fresh artifact. Resume the real deletion. The old age check succeeds at `remote/control.py:317–319`, and the replacement is deleted at `remote/control.py:328` because the deletion guard at `remote/control.py:255–275` checks terminal status and references without verifying age or identity.

## Implementation notes

Bind the destructive eligibility check, job identity, and rename to the same protected decision. An age check must use the generation that will actually be renamed, with the existing fallback for legacy terminal records without `finished_at`. Preserve the submit lock, nonblocking supervisor lease, and active-input guard. Use the deleted generation's metadata for the result.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A deterministic local concurrency regression stages an old prune candidate, replaces it with a fresh completed job under the same ID before deletion, and verifies the replacement state and artifact survive and its bytes are absent from the deletion report. If the implementation serializes the interleaving, verify that the replacement cannot publish until the old operation releases its guard and then remains intact.
- [ ] An old terminal job with no live references is still removed and the report reflects that job's actual finish time and bytes. A fresh or active job and an old terminal job referenced by an active job survive.
- [ ] A disappeared or changed candidate is skipped without aborting cleanup of other eligible jobs. The legacy timestamp fallback has a regression case.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f4468. claim_job performs age, identity, status and rename under the submit lock plus a nonblocking supervisor lease, reporting the renamed generation's finish time and bytes. tests/test_retention.py replacement-race and vanished-candidate regressions. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Bind cancellation to the job generation observed by the request
description:
## Problem

A delayed cancellation can write its marker into a different job that reused the same ID. An unrelated client can lose queued work or a running render after publishing a replacement job.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived interleaving at `ab8753a`. The first client observes job `shot-preview` as running at `remote/control.py:415–416` and pauses. The job completes or is cancelled by another client, which deletes it and submits a replacement with the same ID. The first client's `touch()` at `remote/control.py:417–418` resolves the name again, placing a cancel marker in the replacement directory. The worker consumes the marker at `remote/control.py:179–181` or `remote/control.py:207–215`.

## Implementation notes

Serialize cancellation's lookup and marker publication with directory replacement, or use a stable handle to the observed generation and fail closed if it disappeared. Preserve the ability to cancel while a supervisor holds its active lease. Keep cancellation idempotent and retain completed results when a cancellation arrives after worker success.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A deterministic local race test pauses cancellation after it selects a job while a second client completes, deletes, and reuses the ID. The replacement has no inherited cancel marker and can complete. A locking implementation can instead prove the replacement cannot interleave with selection and marker publication.
- [ ] A real queued job still cancels before starting a worker. A real running stub worker receives cancellation and repeated requests remain safe.
- [ ] A cancellation that observes an already terminal job reports that state without adding a marker, and late worker success keeps the completed result.
close_reason: Fixed in 6b78a74. cancel() holds submit.lock from status check through marker publication; deletion and resubmission replace directories under the same lock. tests/test_cancel.py pauses cancel after selection and proves the replacement inherits no marker. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Stream artifacts from the generation that passed validation
description:
## Problem

Artifact download and inline view validate one pathname over SSH and later open the same pathname in a separate SSH command. Job deletion and ID reuse can make that second command read an unrelated replacement. A same-sized replacement passes download validation, and an oversized replacement can bypass the inline image size cap.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived interleaving at `ab8753a`. Complete job `shot-preview` with artifact `preview.jpg` or `result.mp4`, then start an artifact transfer. After the remote check returns a path and size from `remote/control.py:426–430`, delete the job and publish a replacement under the same ID with different bytes. `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:286–291` checks extension and size before a separate `cat`; `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:300–310` accepts any transferred bytes matching the previous size.

## Implementation notes

Resolve and open the authorized completed-job artifact for a stable generation. Derive validation metadata and transferred bytes from the same open file or an equivalent generation-bound transfer. Keep inline responses bounded and keep large downloads streaming into a temporary file with atomic publication. Do not keep the global submit lock for the full transfer. Preserve the MCP inputs and result shapes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A local SSH-shim test places a different, same-size artifact at a reused job ID between metadata lookup and transfer. Download returns the originally validated bytes or a clear stale-artifact error and never publishes replacement bytes under the old request.
- [ ] An inline view of a replaced artifact cannot read or return bytes above 10,000,000. A normal completed PNG/JPEG still returns the same inline image content type.
- [ ] A large download remains streamed to disk. A failed or interrupted transfer preserves any prior local destination and leaves no partial file.
- [ ] Artifacts from queued, running, failed, or cancelled jobs and traversal or symlink escapes remain refused. Normal concurrent transfers of distinct jobs still work.
close_reason: Fixed in 251297e. open_artifact/stream_artifact open the completed job's directory and artifact without following symlinks and send a size header plus exactly those bytes from one descriptor; the client enforces limits while reading. tests/test_transfer.py same-size and oversize replacement races via a deterministic interpreter hook. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Stop owned descendants before reporting a job cancelled
description:
## Problem

A job can publish terminal cancellation while its FFmpeg process group still contains a live descendant. That process can keep consuming CPU, writing output, or holding resources after the operator has been told the job stopped.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced locally against `ab8753a` using the real supervisor with a stub runner and isolated runtime. The runner spawned a descendant in its process group that ignored SIGTERM, then the test touched the job's cancel marker. The direct worker exited on SIGTERM, the state reached `cancelled`, and the descendant was still alive. The group TERM at `remote/control.py:209` is followed by a wait on only the direct child at `remote/control.py:211–214`; final cleanup at `remote/control.py:231–235` also depends on that child still running.

## Implementation notes

Track cleanup of the owned process group independently from reaping the direct child. Allow a bounded graceful shutdown, then escalate for surviving group members before terminal publication. Handle the group already disappearing without changing a valid result. Keep unrelated groups outside the signal scope, preserve the GPU lease guarantees, and account for abnormal worker exit. Linux parent-death handling at `remote/engine.py:748–751` applies to the direct worker, so a supervisor crash can also strand grandchildren. Treat Linux supervisor loss as a separate test case from ordinary cancellation and preserve isolation from unrelated processes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A local regression uses a stub worker that dies on TERM and an owned descendant that ignores TERM. The descendant can no longer run or write a heartbeat when status first reports `cancelled`, and the supervisor reaps its direct child.
- [ ] A TERM-responsive process group exits within the graceful window, and an unrelated process group remains running.
- [ ] A queued cancellation starts no worker. A worker that already completed successfully still publishes its result if a late cancel marker arrives.
- [ ] The cancellation regression covers both a GPU-mode stub and a normalize-mode stub, and a subsequent GPU-mode stub can acquire the GPU lock after cancellation.
- [ ] On Linux, a test that kills the supervisor with an owned descendant still active demonstrates that the worker tree stops and orphan reconciliation produces a consistent terminal state.
close_reason: Fixed in 6b78a74. Supervisor starts a guard process that leads a new process group and kills the group when the supervisor pipe closes; on any worker exit the supervisor kills remaining group members and waits before publishing terminal state; 10 s TERM grace. tests/test_cancel.py (GPU and normalize stubs, unrelated group survives, supervisor loss) pass on macOS and the Linux workstation. Residual: if the guard itself is killed independently, descendants beyond the worker are not reaped. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Protect the resolved files an active job actually uses
description:
## Problem

Cleanup can delete an active job's input even though retention is intended to protect it. A running worker can pin the old target of an alias while cleanup resolves the alias to its new target. Upload pruning can also recursively remove a directory containing a referenced file because it compares only the directory path against the exact file references.

## Reproduction and evidence

Two code-derived scenarios at `ab8753a`. First, point an in-base symlink `media/current.mp4` at an old producer's artifact, start a consumer, then redirect the link after the worker has resolved the original path. `remote/common.py:67–74` resolves the input, and render and normalization retain it at `remote/engine.py:498` and `remote/engine.py:667`. Submission persists the original request at `remote/control.py:140`. Cleanup resolves the alias again at `remote/control.py:287`, so the original artifact can pass the guard at `remote/control.py:269–271`. Second, submit a valid file under `uploads/session/clip.mp4`. The exact-membership check at `remote/control.py:345` does not see that `uploads/session` contains an active reference, and `remote/control.py:353–354` removes the whole tree.

## Implementation notes

Capture the resolved paths used by the worker and retention at the same stable point for media, target references, and all source references. Keep raw requests comparable for retries. Check path ancestry for recursive removal with component-aware containment. Handle persisted jobs from before the new reference representation conservatively while they remain active. Preserve the base-directory symlink escape check and avoid protecting a different path merely because its text shares a prefix.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A local test starts a consumer from an alias to a producer artifact, changes the alias to a different existing file while the consumer is active, and verifies that both manual deletion and prune retain the original artifact until the consumer becomes terminal.
- [ ] A local test puts an old active input beneath a nested upload directory. Destructive prune and dry run keep that directory and file. An unreferenced old sibling tree is eligible, and the original tree is eligible after the consumer becomes terminal.
- [ ] Exercise media, target-face, and source-face references. An out-of-base symlink is still rejected, and legacy active job records retain a safe cleanup behavior.
- [ ] Unchanged raw submissions remain idempotent, and an unreferenced old flat upload is still pruned.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f4468. submit writes resolved.json (realpath inputs) before publication; worker opens it; retention protects those paths with component-aware ancestry; active jobs without resolved.json block removal. tests/test_retention.py alias-redirect and nested upload tree cases. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Prevent prune from invalidating a concurrent upload reuse
description:
## Problem

Reusing an identical upload can return a path that prune selected earlier and subsequently deletes. A follow-up job then fails with a missing source, even though upload just reported success. If removal lands earlier, the reuse call can fail during the timestamp refresh.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived interleaving at `ab8753a`. Seed an unreferenced content-addressed file older than the retention cutoff. Pause prune after it selects that file at `remote/control.py:339–346`. Run `find_upload`, which checks the file and refreshes mtime without the prune lock at `remote/control.py:458–469`. Resume prune. Its final unlink at `remote/control.py:350–356` does not recheck age and removes the reused file. If prune unlinks between the check and touch, the timestamp refresh raises instead of returning a normal cache miss.

## Implementation notes

Make the cache-hit check and timestamp refresh atomic with respect to the cleanup decision, using the existing retention lock or an equivalent identity-and-age recheck. If deletion wins, a cache miss should allow the caller to perform a normal upload. Preserve hash and size checks. Keep streaming outside long-held shared locks. This coordinates a simultaneous reuse and prune while retaining documented age-based cleanup for later prune invocations.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A deterministic local concurrency test coordinates a prune and reuse of the same old upload. If reuse wins, that prune retains the refreshed upload and reports no deletion for it.
- [ ] If prune wins, reuse returns a cache miss and the client can upload again successfully. There is no stale success response or unhandled missing-file error.
- [ ] Ordinary identical uploads still avoid sending bytes, recent uses are kept, and an untouched unreferenced old upload still gets pruned.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f4468. find_upload's cache-hit check and timestamp refresh run under the retention lock; deletion winning yields a cache miss. tests/test_retention.py prune-wins and reuse-wins regressions. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Continue pruning when an upload publishes during the scan
description:
## Problem

A successful upload can rename away its temporary file while prune is scanning. The resulting missing-file exception aborts the entire prune. Some terminal jobs may already be deleted before the error, leaving the caller without an accurate report.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived interleaving at `ab8753a`. Start an upload and pause prune after the upload directory glob includes its `.partial` file. Resume the upload through `os.replace` at `remote/control.py:492`, which removes that pathname as part of publication. Resume prune before the unguarded `lstat` at `remote/control.py:339–340`. The stale name raises `FileNotFoundError`; prune may already have performed job deletions at `remote/control.py:328`.

## Implementation notes

Tolerate entries that disappear during enumeration as a normal concurrent publication or cleanup outcome. Keep unrelated filesystem errors distinguishable. Coordinate candidate checks with final publication where necessary so an old candidate cannot cause removal of a different freshly published file. Preserve temporary-file integrity and the existing stale-partial age rule.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A deterministic local test renames a `.partial` file to its completed upload name between enumeration and metadata lookup. Prune returns normally, accurately reports any prior eligible job removals, and leaves the newly published upload intact.
- [ ] Exercise both dry-run and destructive modes. An unrelated old upload is processed normally even when a transient pathname disappears.
- [ ] An actually stale partial remains eligible, a recent in-flight partial is retained, and normal upload publication still verifies size and hash.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f4468. Prune tolerates vanished .partial entries and keeps other filesystem errors visible. tests/test_retention.py publishes an upload between enumeration and lstat in dry-run and destructive modes. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Exclude actively referenced producers from prune previews
description:
## Problem

The default dry run reports old producer jobs and their bytes as removable even while a queued or running consumer depends on their artifacts. The corresponding destructive prune refuses those jobs, so the preview overstates the expected removals.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced locally against `ab8753a` with isolated job state and the real prune path. Seed an old completed producer with a normalized video or crop and a running consumer whose request references it. Dry-run prune lists the producer. Destructive prune leaves it in place and omits it from its result. Dry-run reporting builds entries directly at `remote/control.py:321–326`, while destructive cleanup delegates at `remote/control.py:328` to the active-reference guard at `remote/control.py:269–271`.

## Implementation notes

Use the same eligibility rules for previews and deletion, including the active-input guard and appropriate handling of the supervisor lease and changed or disappeared candidates. Preserve dry-run behavior and the existing report schema. Compute totals from the eligible entries while accounting for the fact that later invocations can see different live state.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With unchanged state and time, dry run and destructive prune return identical eligible job IDs and byte totals for an old referenced producer, an old unreferenced producer, and a fresh producer.
- [ ] Repeat the protected producer case with queued and running consumers using media and face-reference artifacts. Confirm the producer becomes eligible after those consumers become terminal.
- [ ] Dry run leaves all job directories and artifacts in place, and destructive prune still deletes only eligible jobs.
close_reason: Fixed in 13f4468. Dry run uses the same claim_job eligibility with remove=False. tests/test_retention.py compares dry-run and destructive results for referenced, unreferenced and fresh producers with queued and running consumers. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Seek CFR frames and audio on the video stream timeline
description:
## Problem

The render checks video presentation timestamps but calculates FFmpeg input seeks as if the container and selected video stream share a start. An earlier audio stream can shift the seek origin. A partial job can swap the wrong frames and still pass frame count and duration checks.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with a 25 fps CFR MKV whose video starts at PTS 0 and audio starts at −0.423 s. The packet timing check accepted all 25 frames. A seek for frame 14 returned sequential frame 3, and requests for frames 1 through 10 returned frame 0. The actual partial render encode and mux completed with a pass-through Fusion stub.

`remote/engine.py:156-163` supplies a relative input `-ss` without accounting for the container origin. `remote/engine.py:467-494` checks only video packet timestamps. `remote/engine.py:562-593` makes a second relative seek when selecting source audio.

## Implementation notes

Use the selected video stream's verified timestamp origin consistently for random-access decode, partial render boundaries and audio trim. Preserve the efficient seek path when practical. Compare content or timestamps of the selected frames to a sequential reference in tests, since matching only the count misses the regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For the earlier-audio CFR MKV, requesting frame 14 returns the same pixels as sequential frame 14. Check at least one earlier nonzero index as well.
- [ ] A partial render of frames 14 through 18 processes exactly those source frames and selects the corresponding source-audio interval.
- [ ] The regular zero-start CFR path, frame-zero behavior, fractional CFR rates and out-of-range error behavior remain covered.
- [ ] Audio absence or partial overlap is handled separately from the seek origin so the selected video range remains correct in both cases.
close_reason: Fixed in 3864aa6. decode and the render audio input seek with -seek_timestamp 1 on the video stream clock. tests/test_timing.py compares selected frames to a sequential decode on an MKV with audio at -0.423 s and checks a partial render 14-18 selects exact frames and the matching audio interval. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Return persisted jobs on identical retries after input cleanup
description:
## Problem

An identical retry can fail after the original media or references are moved or pruned even though the completed job and its result still exist. This breaks the documented stable job-ID reconnect contract.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived scenario at `ab8753a`. Complete job `shot-preview` from an upload. Remove that input after the job is terminal while keeping the job directory. Repeat the same submission payload and ID. `remote/control.py:132` calls `validate_request` before checking the persisted request at `remote/control.py:133–136`. The live input check at `remote/common.py:163` raises first. Layout validation and target/source input checks can fail on the same retry at `remote/common.py:196–210`.

## Implementation notes

Under the existing submit lock, handle an existing ID and compare its immutable request before consulting mutable resources. Keep meaningful conflict detection, including changed payload types, and avoid starting a second supervisor. Continue live validation under the submit lock for new jobs to preserve synchronization with retention. Maintain compatibility with existing persisted requests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Complete a local job with a stored result, delete its input, and retry the exact request. The reply still includes the original completed job and result and no new supervisor starts.
- [ ] An exact retry also succeeds if the Fusion layout files have become unavailable after the original job. A different payload under the same ID still reports a request conflict when its input is missing.
- [ ] A new job with the missing input still fails validation without publishing a job directory. Concurrent identical submissions still produce a single worker.
close_reason: Fixed in f9a1d03. Under the submit lock an existing ID is answered from its persisted request (canonical JSON) before live validation. tests/test_submit.py retries after input and layout removal, conflicts and concurrent identical submits. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Record a stable finish time for reconciled and launch-failed jobs
description:
## Problem

Jobs that fail during orphan reconciliation or supervisor launch can lack a finish timestamp. Their reported elapsed time then keeps growing while their status remains terminal.

## Reproduction and evidence

Code-derived at `ab8753a`. Seed an old nonterminal job with no supervisor lease and query its state, or inject a supervisor launch failure. Reconciliation at `remote/control.py:50–52` and launch-failure handling at `remote/control.py:160–163` publish `failed` without `finished_at`. The list calculation falls back to the current clock at `remote/control.py:105–114`. Listing twice at different times therefore gives two elapsed values for the same failed job.

## Implementation notes

Record the finish time when these paths publish terminal status. For old persisted terminal states with no timestamp, derive a stable value from existing persisted metadata, with a documented fallback that works for retention as well. Preserve increasing elapsed time for active jobs and keep existing terminal error text and state semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A local orphan-reconciliation regression verifies the persisted `failed` state includes `finished_at`; job status and two list calls at different simulated times report the same terminal duration.
- [ ] An injected supervisor-launch failure also persists a finish timestamp and reports a fixed terminal duration. The original launch error remains available.
- [ ] A preexisting terminal record without `finished_at` reports a stable duration and remains subject to the intended retention policy, while elapsed time for queued and running jobs continues to advance.
close_reason: Fixed in 6b78a74. Orphan reconciliation and launch failure persist finished_at; legacy terminal records report state.json mtime via current(). tests/test_cancel.py stable-duration regressions. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Fail deployment when an active-job query fails
description:
## Problem

A normal deployment can proceed after the queued-job query fails. The running-job query can then succeed and return an empty result, causing the script to conclude that no jobs are active. The deployment guard must establish both states before any release is copied or published.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Verified with a local Bash equivalent at review commit `ab8753a`. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the queued command in the left-hand `for` pipeline returned nonzero with no output, the running command emitted `{"result":[]}`, and the guard received an empty string and exited successfully.
- The pipeline at `scripts/deploy.sh:10–19` takes the exit status of the final loop iteration, so `pipefail` does not report a failed earlier iteration. The JSON parser also accepts an empty input stream. Copy and publication follow at `scripts/deploy.sh:20–30`.
- The review used a local shell model. No deployment or workstation request was performed.

## Implementation notes

Check each required SSH exit status and response independently, or query both states in one operation that returns a single explicit result. Distinguish the expected first-install case from a failed or malformed response from an existing installation. Fail before copying files when the state is uncertain, with a message that identifies the failed status query or remote error. Preserve intentional `--force` behavior. The separate deployment locking issue covers job and release races after a successful check.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With a local SSH shim, a failed queued query with empty stdout followed by a successful empty running query aborts a non-forced deployment before any release directory creation, upload or symlink change.
- [ ] A failure in the running query, an invalid JSON response, an error envelope or a missing response from an installed control script also aborts with a diagnostic.
- [ ] A nonempty queued or running response aborts a normal deployment and reports the relevant job IDs.
- [ ] A valid idle installation and an explicitly confirmed first install can proceed. A deliberate `--force` invocation retains the documented override.
- [ ] Regression coverage uses local shims with no workstation or GPU dependency.

title: Coordinate deployment with job submission and pin release code
description:
## Problem

A client can submit a job after deployment checks for active jobs but before the release switch. A control process that started through the old symlink can also resolve `__file__` after a switch and launch its supervisor from the new release. Two concurrent deployers share the same `remote.next` path and can publish the wrong candidate or fail while swapping it.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Pause deployment after the checks at `scripts/deploy.sh:12–19`, submit a job, then resume through `scripts/deploy.sh:22–29`. The script does not recheck under a lock shared with submission.
- Pause submission after it loaded the existing release and before the supervisor spawn. Switch the `remote` symlink, then resume. The spawn resolves the mutable link at `remote/control.py:151–159`; validation ran earlier at `remote/control.py:129–132`.
- Interleave two publish commands after the first writes `remote.next` and before it moves it. The second replaces the first staged link at `scripts/deploy.sh:27`.
- The existing release test switches the symlink after `submit` returns, so it does not cover a switch during submission. See `tests/test_jobs.py:351–371`. No live concurrent deployment was performed during review.

## Implementation notes

Coordinate the final active-job check, promotion and release cleanup with submission using a workstation-side lock or equivalent ordering. Keep staging unique and make each publish command verify and promote its own completed candidate. Anchor each control invocation to an immutable release early enough that the supervisor and its engine use the same release as submission. Coordinate forced release cleanup with live release ownership so forced promotion cannot remove files that an active job will still open. Retain initial-install and legacy-directory handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Deterministic tests pause a deployer and a submitter at the race boundaries. A normal deployment either observes the queued or running job and refuses, or the submission begins against the newly promoted release.
- [ ] When the symlink changes after a control invocation starts, the invocation and its supervisor/engine use a consistent release or the invocation cleanly retries against the current release.
- [ ] Two concurrent deploys of distinguishable candidates cannot clobber each other's staging link or report successful promotion of a different candidate. A failed copy or promotion keeps the previous release selectable and returns nonzero.
- [ ] Cleanup preserves every release an active job will still need, including on the forced path. The currently selected release is never removed.
- [ ] Ordinary deploy, first install, and migration from a legacy real directory have local regression coverage.

title: Decouple normalization request validation from Fusion layout files
description:
## Problem

CPU-only normalization still needs the Fusion checkout's UI layout files. The shared request validator loads them for every job kind, although normalization has no Fusion controls or mappings. Missing or temporarily unreadable layout files can reject valid normalization before FFmpeg starts, either at submission or again during worker startup.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Point `VM_APP` at a temporary directory with no Fusion layout files and keep a valid clip under `VM_BASE`. Submitting `normalize_media` reaches `remote/control.py:124–132` and then the unconditional `layouts()` at `remote/common.py:193–198`.
- `layouts()` reads Fusion files at `remote/common.py:95–101`. The same validator runs in `remote/engine.py:747–756` immediately before the branch that dispatches normalization without initializing Fusion. A missing layout therefore blocks either boundary.
- This was traced from source. No live normalization was run with a missing app checkout.

## Implementation notes

Keep the shared input path and rate validation, but separate the settings and mapping validation that actually needs Fusion metadata from the normalization path. If the raw control protocol accepts unexpected GPU-only fields for normalization today, give those fields an explicit policy that needs no layout read. Keep the worker's current runner contract and GPU-independent dispatch intact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Using a local temporary backend with a working test runner and no Fusion layout files, a valid normalization request passes both submission and worker validation and produces a result.
- [ ] A worker revalidating an already-queued normalization request still proceeds when the Fusion layout files have become unavailable.
- [ ] An invalid FPS, missing source or source escaping the allowed path roots still fails with the corresponding validation error.
- [ ] Detect, preview and render retain their existing Fusion settings and mapping validation, including rejection of unsupported keys.
- [ ] The regression proves that normalization does not read Fusion layouts or initialize GPU models.
close_reason: Fixed in f9a1d03. validate_fusion_request carries settings/mapping checks for detect/preview/render; normalize requests may only carry kind, media_path, fps and never read layouts; load_config no longer requires layout files. tests/test_submit.py runs normalization end to end without layouts. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Allow generated and uploaded media when state is outside the media root
description:
## Problem

The documented `VM_STATE` override can point at a separate storage directory. Uploads and normalization then succeed and return absolute paths under that directory, but later media and mapping validation rejects those same paths because they are outside `VM_BASE`.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Start a local backend with `VM_BASE=/tmp/example-media` and `VM_STATE=/tmp/example-runtime`. Upload a valid image, then pass its returned path to detection or as a swap reference. Alternatively, normalize a clip from the media root and submit the returned `media_path` to a new job.
- `remote/common.py:13–15` resolves the settings independently, while `remote/common.py:67–74` confines inputs to `BASE`. Uploads are published under `STATE/uploads` at `remote/control.py:440–455`, and normalization returns the path under the job artifact directory at `remote/engine.py:724–727`. Configuration is documented at `README.md:106–119`.
- No real workstation path configuration was changed during review.

## Implementation notes

Support consumable media in the managed upload and job-artifact directories when runtime storage sits outside `VM_BASE`. Use canonical paths and validate the managed subdirectory boundaries, including their ancestors and any symlink targets. Avoid admitting the whole external state tree, which also contains manifests, worker logs and locks. Keep application and runner configuration independent of this path policy. Document supported placement and retained restrictions.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With separate temporary `VM_BASE` and `VM_STATE` roots, upload returns an image path that works as media and as a target/source face reference.
- [ ] A normalized artifact under external state can be inspected and passed to a subsequent detect or render submission.
- [ ] The default nested-state layout and ordinary source media under `VM_BASE` continue to work.
- [ ] Files in unrelated locations and non-artifact files in the external state tree are rejected. Traversal and symlinks cannot extend the approved roots.
- [ ] A local integration fixture exercises producer-to-consumer handoff without relying on a live workstation.
close_reason: Fixed in f9a1d03. state_dir may lie outside media_root; input_path admits only complete uploads and job artifacts files from the state tree. tests/test_submit.py producer-to-consumer integration with external state and a rejection matrix. Follow-up: artifacts of non-completed jobs are accepted by path. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Confine local artifact downloads and return an absolute path
description:
## Problem

`download_artifact` trusts a preexisting local job directory to be inside the configured downloads root. If that directory is a symlink to another directory, streaming and atomic replacement occur at the symlink target. In addition, a configured root containing a literal tilde or relative path is kept as-is and the API can return a relative path despite its contract.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Set the downloads root to a temporary directory and make its `done` child a symlink to a second directory containing a sentinel `result.mp4`. Request the completed `done` job's artifact via the local SSH shim. The derived destination follows the symlink and can replace the sentinel.
- Set `VISOMASTER_DOWNLOADS` to the literal value `~/downloads/example` or a relative directory. `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:19–21` creates a `Path` without expanding or making it absolute. The returned path is `str(destination)` at `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:300–313`, despite the absolute-path promise at line 298.
- These scenarios were identified by tracing filesystem operations. The review did not overwrite any local file.

## Implementation notes

Expand and anchor the configured downloads root once using an explicit policy for relative paths. Treat the configured root as the trusted boundary and keep the job directory, temporary file, final replace and cleanup within it, including concurrent directory replacement. Use directory-relative filesystem operations with no-follow checks if needed to enforce that boundary throughout a streamed transfer. Preserve direct streaming and atomic publication of validated bytes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A local test with a symlinked job directory pointing outside the configured root fails safely and preserves the external sentinel file and directory.
- [ ] A deterministic test replaces or renames the job directory during transfer. The operation either publishes within the validated download root or fails safely, with no external write.
- [ ] A tilde-prefixed override expands to the user's home directory. A supported relative override is anchored predictably, or rejected with a clear configuration error. Every successful result returns an absolute path.
- [ ] Normal downloads still stream to a temporary file, verify byte count, atomically replace an existing artifact and remove temporary files on failure.
close_reason: Fixed in 251297e. Downloads root opened once; temp file in the root; job dir opened O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW relative to it; publish with dir-fd os.replace; ~ expands and relative roots are rejected; results absolute. tests/test_transfer.py symlink, swap and rename-during-transfer cases. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Reject explicitly empty job IDs across submission tools
description:
## Problem

An empty `job_id` is silently replaced with a random UUID. Repeated calls with the same empty ID can create several jobs, even though the backend's ID rules reject empty strings and the caller may believe it is sending a stable ID.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Submit the same valid request twice with `job_id: ""`. The client evaluates `job_id or uuid.uuid4().hex` in `detect_faces`, `submit_swap` and `normalize_media` at `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:149`, `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:182` and `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:211`.
- The backend receives two generated IDs, so the existing `remote/common.py:61–64` validation never sees the invalid input.
- This was identified by source inspection. No jobs were submitted during review.

## Implementation notes

Generate an ID only for the omitted or null argument. Pass an explicit invalid value to the existing canonical validation or reject it equivalently at the API boundary. Apply the same behavior to detection, preview, render and normalization. Keep existing IDs and request payloads compatible.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Local submission tests cover detection, preview, render and normalization. An explicit empty ID returns a validation error and creates no job directory or worker.
- [ ] Omitted and null IDs still generate valid IDs.
- [ ] A valid explicit ID is preserved exactly. An identical retry returns the existing job, and changed settings under that ID remain a conflict.
- [ ] The user-facing tool schema or documentation describes the allowed format where practical.
close_reason: Fixed in f9a1d03. Clients generate an ID only for omitted/null job_id; explicit values go to backend validation, so empty IDs are rejected for detect, preview, render and normalize. tests/test_submit.py through the stdio server. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Make health compatibility reflect tracked Fusion app changes
description:
## Problem

Health reports `compatible: true` for a Fusion checkout at the supported commit even if tracked files under `app` have changed. The worker rejects the same checkout, so the recommended first check can report compatibility immediately before valid GPU jobs fail at startup.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Use a temporary Git checkout at the configured supported revision, modify a tracked file inside `app`, and compare the health result with worker startup.
- `remote/control.py:363–385` calculates compatibility from the commit SHA. `remote/engine.py:30–42` also runs `git diff HEAD -- app` and raises before loading Fusion when it finds tracked changes.
- The review traced the two code paths. It did not alter the installed Fusion checkout.

## Implementation notes

Reuse the same standard-library compatibility check for health and worker startup so the accepted revision and tracked-file policy agree. Preserve existing health fields and add an actionable reason or check detail for dirty app files and unsupported revisions. Keep the deployed-adapter hash check separate. Health should still report available diagnostics when the compatibility check identifies an unsupported checkout.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For the supported revision with clean tracked app files, health reports compatible and the shared guard permits initialization.
- [ ] Modified tracked app content, including a staged modification present on disk, makes health report incompatible with a dirty-app reason and triggers the same startup guard.
- [ ] An unsupported revision reports an explicit revision reason. A change outside the guarded app scope follows the existing startup policy.
- [ ] Existing revision, GPU and adapter code-hash fields remain usable. Automated tests use temporary Git fixtures or command stubs without loading Fusion or using the GPU.
close_reason: Fixed in f9a1d03. common.fusion_compatibility is shared by health and worker startup; health adds compatibility_reason. tests/test_submit.py uses temporary Git checkouts for clean, staged/unstaged/deleted app changes and unsupported revisions. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Verify deployed code and distinguish skipped cancellation in the GPU smoke test
description:
## Problem

The GPU smoke script can generate qualification evidence against stale deployed adapter code because it checks only Fusion compatibility. The check can also count queued cancellation as proof of running cancellation because it never asserts that the job reached running. Its cancellation check assumes the disconnect test render stays active through session teardown and reconnection. A short clip or slow reconnect can complete normally before cancellation, producing a false failure and no clear indication of which behavior was exercised.

## Reproduction and evidence

- Inferred from the reviewed code at `ab8753a`. Stub a health response with `compatible: true` and `code_matches: false`. The script continues past the check at `scripts/smoke_gpu.py:46–51`, even though the hash comparison is already available at `src/visomaster_mcp/server.py:95–112`.
- Let the render submitted at `scripts/smoke_gpu.py:90–98` finish before the second session reaches `scripts/smoke_gpu.py:100–104`. `remote/control.py:414–423` correctly leaves a terminal job unchanged, while the smoke script unconditionally asserts `cancelled`.
- These cases were traced from code. No smoke test or GPU job was run during review.

## Implementation notes

Gate qualification on a confirmed code match and fail clearly before queuing any work if hashes differ or are unavailable. Record the release and hash status. Keep reconnection and cancellation evidence separate. Observe the job state before and after the cancellation request. Record queued cancellation separately and require evidence of a running worker for a running-cancellation pass. If it completes first, report cancellation as unexercised with the reason, or use a controlled workload to guarantee it is still active. Use explicit checks for the touched qualification gates so optimized Python does not omit them.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-session tests show a mismatched or unknown code hash causes a clear preflight failure before a detection or render submission. A match allows the workflow to proceed and is recorded in evidence.
- [ ] If the disconnect render completes before cancellation, the script verifies the reconnected session found the job and records that cancellation was unexercised. The evidence cannot be mistaken for a cancellation pass.
- [ ] If a running worker is observed before cancellation and the final state is cancelled, evidence records running cancellation as passed. A queued cancellation is recorded separately. An unexpected failed job or a timeout still yields an actionable failure.
- [ ] A controlled local test covers both reconnect outcomes without a GPU. The existing opt-in real GPU invocation continues to work with the documented fixture inputs.
close_reason: Fixed in 06b2209. smoke_gpu.py gates on code_matches before any submission, records preflight evidence, classifies cancellation as passed/passed_queued/unexercised, and uses explicit checks instead of assert. tests/test_smoke.py (19) with a fake session. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Resolve detection and preview frame indices correctly on VFR inputs
description:
## Problem

Detection and preview take a zero-based frame index. They currently convert that ordinal to an input timestamp using average FPS. When actual frame spacing varies, different indices can return the same image and the job can label a face crop with the wrong frame number.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with a 15-frame MP4 produced by dropping a block of frames from a 25 fps source while retaining timestamps. A sequential decode gave the actual frame order. Index 2 returned frame 3, and indices 3, 4, 5 and 8 all returned frame 5.

`remote/engine.py:152-163` converts an ordinal into an average-rate seek timestamp. `remote/engine.py:180-195` calls it for detection and preview without the render's timing check. Multi-frame detection calls the same path at `remote/engine.py:277-286`.

## Implementation notes

For every supported media path, select by actual decoded frame ordinal or validate the assumptions required by the CFR fast path before seeking. If VFR frame indexing remains outside the supported media contract, give the same normalization guidance in all three detection and preview paths before returning any mislabeled artifact. Keep the public frame index zero-based.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] On the uneven-timestamp fixture, explicit frame requests return the expected ordinal pixels or a clear instruction to normalize. None succeeds with the wrong frame.
- [ ] Single-frame detection, multi-frame detection and previews follow the same VFR behavior.
- [ ] An index equal to the number of decoded frames receives an out-of-range error. Normalizing the fixture produces a CFR file whose valid indices work consistently.
- [ ] Existing still-image frame-zero and CFR frame-selection behavior remains verified.
close_reason: Fixed in 3864aa6. load_frame maps the zero-based ordinal through the video packet timestamps (timeline()), so VFR detection, multi-frame sampling and preview return the exact decoded frame; index == frame count is out of range. Covered by test_timing.py VFR fixtures through engine.run. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Use video-specific extent for sampling and normalization
description:
## Problem

The container's duration can be governed by a longer audio track, and some readable sources provide no duration metadata. Treating that metadata as video extent generates invalid detection indices and can reject a complete normalization after FFmpeg succeeds.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with a 25 fps MKV containing 1 s of video and 3 s of audio. FFprobe reported no video-stream frame count or duration. Five requested samples yielded indices 7, 22, 37, 52 and 67, even though only the first 25 frames exist. Normalization encoded the full video and failed with `Normalized output has 25 frames, expected about 76`. A valid 25-frame raw H.264 input with no reported duration failed against a one-frame estimate.

`remote/engine.py:265-272` computes detection sampling from container duration if the video frame count is absent. `remote/engine.py:677-678` and `remote/engine.py:719-720` use container duration or a one-frame default as a hard normalization validation baseline.

## Implementation notes

Derive the extent of the selected video stream from trustworthy video metadata or a bounded timeline or frame scan when metadata is missing. Keep estimated progress separate from validated completeness. Preserve checks for malformed, empty or incomplete video output. Establish an explicit contract for representing unknown totals before a reliable count is available.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Sampling five times across the 25-frame MKV returns distinct, valid indices from the selected video stream and completes.
- [ ] The MKV normalizes to the correct video extent even with the longer audio track. No whole-container estimate can independently fail the job.
- [ ] A supported video source without reliable duration metadata completes when output validation establishes a complete result. Empty or truncated output still fails.
- [ ] Regression coverage includes a file with exact video frame metadata, missing video duration, and missing container duration, and verifies progress reports do not claim an incorrect authoritative total.
close_reason: Fixed in 3864aa6. Sampling counts the video stream's own frames; normalization's expected count comes from video_extent (stream duration or timestamp scan), never container duration; progress reports estimated_total_frames, null when unknown. test_timing.py covers exact, missing video duration and missing container duration. Raw H.264 is no longer an accepted container (qpn.1), so that case uses a stripped probe. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Accept valid video intervals when the selected audio track has no overlap
description:
## Problem

Render and normalize require an audio track whenever the source contains one, even if the chosen source audio has no samples in the requested video interval. The result can be valid video with legitimately empty audio, but the job fails and withholds the artifact.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with a one-second, 25 fps MP4 whose first AAC stream ends around 0.3 s. A render of frames 15–19 using a pass-through Fusion stub failed with `Audio missing from output`. In a separate MP4 whose audio starts around 1.48 s after its one-second video ends, normalization failed with `Audio missing from normalized output`.

`remote/engine.py:600-609` bases the render check and result audio field on source stream existence. `remote/engine.py:657-661` trims normalization audio, while `remote/engine.py:721-742` still expects a track whenever one existed anywhere in the source.

## Implementation notes

Determine audio expectations from the first selected audio stream's overlap with the video interval. Permit a successful result when there are no samples to preserve and report the audio actually emitted. Preserve alignment when part of the first stream overlaps. Keep genuine audio loss and mux errors visible when samples were expected.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A render wholly after the first audio track ends completes with the selected video frames and an audio manifest that matches the output file.
- [ ] A normalization whose first audio starts after video ends completes with the validated video and an accurate audio manifest.
- [ ] A partially overlapping delayed track retains its timing relative to video. An overlapping track that disappears because of a mux or encoding failure still fails clearly.
- [ ] A source with multiple audio streams follows the existing first-audio selection contract and a source with no audio continues to complete.
close_reason: Fixed in a777ad8. audio_overlaps decides audio expectation from the first audio stream's overlap with the video interval; no overlap yields audio: none, lost expected audio still fails. tests/test_audio.py, passing on FFmpeg 8.1 and 6.1. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Trim normalized audio to the resampled output video endpoint
description:
## Problem

Normalization trims audio using source video duration, which can differ from the duration after frame-rate resampling. When video duration metadata is absent, the audio filter also omits its end bound. The job validates video timing and audio presence without validating the relationship between their endpoints.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` by normalizing a 1.44 s, 25 fps MP4 with matching audio to 1 fps. The job succeeded and the MP4 contained 1.0 s of video and 1.44 s of audio. The missing-metadata case follows from the conditional trim in source and is separate from the reproduced rate-change case.

`remote/engine.py:647-661` builds the audio end from the original stream duration. `remote/engine.py:715-725` validates the resampled video but only checks whether the output audio stream exists.

## Implementation notes

Bound the output audio by the actual normalized video interval after resampling, including sources with no reported stream duration. Keep sample alignment at the video start and account for AAC packetization or encoder delay when verifying the endpoint. Preserve the video frame count and rate if the source audio is shorter.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For the 1.44 s source normalized to 1 fps, the video stays one second and audio ends within one encoded AAC frame of the video endpoint.
- [ ] When the selected video has no duration tag and the first audio track extends beyond it, normalized audio is also bounded by the resulting video endpoint.
- [ ] Earlier and delayed audio fixtures retain the correct relative timing at the start, and shorter audio does not truncate normalized video.
- [ ] The returned manifest and FFprobe both describe the published tracks accurately.
close_reason: Fixed in a777ad8. Normalization encodes video first, then muxes audio over exactly frames/rate; output_audio fails if audio overruns the video by more than one AAC frame; result gains audio_duration. tests/test_audio.py covers the 1.44 s at 1 fps case and duration-less MKV. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Convert RGB-tagged video to valid YUV color metadata
description:
## Problem

Both H.264 output paths use a YUV pixel format but pass through the input color-space name verbatim. For RGB video FFprobe reports `gbr`, which the FFmpeg encoder option parser rejects. Even an accepted spelling for the RGB identity matrix would misdescribe pixels converted to YUV.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with a synthetic MP4 encoded using `libx264rgb`. FFprobe reported `pix_fmt=gbrp`, `color_space=gbr` and full range. Normalization failed because `-colorspace gbr` could not be parsed. The render exposure follows from its use of the same color-tag helper.

`remote/engine.py:128-149` encodes BGR render frames as YUV and builds tags from the input stream. `remote/engine.py:653-656` applies the same helper to normalization.

## Implementation notes

Choose an output color matrix and range consistent with the actual RGB-to-YUV conversion and apply them explicitly on both paths. Preserve applicable transfer and primary metadata and the established SDR policy. Compare decoded color patches so acceptance catches a successful encode with incorrect tags or visibly shifted color.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An SDR libx264rgb MP4 normalizes and renders with the pass-through worker fixture without a color option parse error.
- [ ] FFprobe reports a valid YUV pixel format and matrix for both outputs. Known-color patches survive an RGB-to-YUV round trip within codec-appropriate tolerance.
- [ ] Tagged BT.709 limited- and full-range YUV fixtures retain the current matrix, range and tag behavior. HDR rejection remains covered.
close_reason: Fixed in 71b7907. RGB sources decode without a matrix at full range and encode as BT.709 limited on render and normalize; color tags are set on frames via setparams since FFmpeg 8 drops -color_primaries/-color_trc encoder options. tests/test_color.py patch round trips within +/-4 on FFmpeg 8.1 and 6.1. Follow-up: ycgco/bt2020c-style source matrices fail to convert under FFmpeg 8. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Recognize high-bit-depth formats beyond planar YUV suffixes
description:
## Problem

The output depth decision matches only pixel-format names ending in a planar `p10le`-style suffix. Valid high-bit-depth formats outside that naming pattern are treated as eight-bit. Normalization then silently loses precision even when the actual input is ten-bit.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with an FFV1 MKV encoded as `gray10le`. The input probed as 10-bit, and normalization completed with `yuvj420p`, an eight-bit output. Packed and semiplanar names such as `rgb48le` and `p010le` also miss the source predicate. Their end-to-end behavior was inferred from source inspection.

`remote/engine.py:124-131` decides render depth from the format string. `remote/engine.py:653-655` uses the same decision for normalization.

## Implementation notes

Base the depth decision on authoritative component depth from FFmpeg pixel-format descriptors or trustworthy stream metadata. Treat metadata with absent or zero depth as unknown and resolve from the actual decoded format. Keep the documented H.264 output policy of 10-bit for sources above eight bits. Keep the separate eight-bit Fusion processing boundary explicit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A gray10le FFV1 MKV normalizes to yuv420p10le and retains the expected range.
- [ ] Depth classification tests cover gray10le, at least one packed or semiplanar format, yuv420p10le and representative eight-bit input.
- [ ] Render and normalization choose the same ten-bit encode policy for a supported high-depth input. Eight-bit sources still encode as eight-bit.
- [ ] Normalization of a ten-bit gradient retains distinctions finer than eight-bit quantization at the existing codec quality setting.
close_reason: Fixed in 71b7907. Depth comes from bits_per_raw_sample or the decoded pixel-format descriptor's deepest component; render and normalize share the policy. tests/test_color.py covers gray10le, p010le, rgb48be, y210le, yuv420p10le and 8-bit, plus a 10-bit ramp keeping >32 levels. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Preserve video display aspect and handle reflected display matrices
description:
## Problem

The raw BGR pipe carries raster dimensions but loses sample aspect ratio. Anamorphic footage is therefore exported with a different display aspect. The adapter also looks only for nonzero rotation, so a reflected display matrix can pass validation and be dropped, changing the orientation of the result.

## Reproduction and evidence

Locally reproduced at `ab8753a` with actual FFmpeg encoding and a pass-through Fusion stub. A 96×64 source with a 4:3 sample aspect ratio rendered successfully with unspecified output SAR, interpreted as square pixels. A separate input remuxed with FFmpeg's `-display_vflip` reported a reflected display matrix with rotation zero and also rendered successfully without that matrix.

`remote/engine.py:82-88` tests only the rotation scalar. `remote/engine.py:128-136` rebuilds the stream from raw raster dimensions without SAR. `remote/engine.py:157-164` disables autorotation in decode.

## Implementation notes

Preserve source sample aspect ratio on the render output when the pixel geometry is unchanged. Inspect the actual display transformation, including flips whose rotation angle is zero. Route transforms the adapter cannot represent to normalization with a clear error. Verify rendered display geometry using both probe metadata and an asymmetric fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A 96×64 source tagged with SAR 4:3 retains its source display aspect after a partial and a full render.
- [ ] A vertical-reflection display matrix with rotation zero is either applied consistently or refused with normalization guidance before artifacts are published.
- [ ] After normalization, an asymmetric marker confirms the reflected source orientation is correct. The existing rotated-video and square-pixel behavior remains covered.
close_reason: Fixed in 71b7907. Render output carries and validates source SAR; display_transform() reads the display matrix and render/detect/preview refuse rotations or flips with normalize guidance; normalization applies flips (reflection_applied in result). tests/test_color.py marker and aspect fixtures; muxed audio keeps tags and SAR. Full suite 345 passed, 1 skipped; Ruff clean.

title: Reap worker descendants if the cancellation guard process dies independently
description: The supervisor's guard process kills the job's process group when the supervisor dies. If the guard itself is killed separately (for example by the OOM killer), the worker still dies via PR_SET_PDEATHSIG but its descendants are not reaped. Consider recording the pgid with an ownership check so orphan reconciliation can stop survivors, or a subreaper. Residual from vmcp-review-remediation-qpn.15.
